governing_text: An Extraction, the analysis of one paragraph under passages/FORMAT.md, is the source of every paragraph Move, and it is written by a fixed row on the shared supervisor with a run record rather than by a session, so that a wrong Move can be traced to the Extraction or to the ingest and the stage can be run again on the same input. [implemented-against: passages/FORMAT.md "The paragraph unit", copied 2026-10-15]

The row belongs to the Proof Sheet and changes no production executable; whether a production Extractor adopts it is a separate decision.

judge.note: Every unit is a headless session, a `claude -p` child that runs with no tools (`--tools ""`), spawned by the shared Detached Job supervisor (src/workflow/detached-job.mjs). The model and both bounds NAME THE BRIEF'S SETTINGS, because the Issue gives this row the same bounds as the Brief's. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` replaces the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY.

job.note: ONE JOB PER PARAGRAPH, ONE UNIT PER JOB, run in the Leg's order: paragraph N's input carries the reader state paragraph N-1's Extraction left, so N cannot start before N-1 is written. A call past `brief.call_limit_s` is stopped and spends one attempt, a refused answer spends one, an unreadable answer is asked again without spending one, and a paragraph that has spent `brief.unit_attempts` stops the run naming the paragraph and its last refusal; the Extractions already written stay.

extraction_unit.note: The one call per paragraph (kogaki#1384). `src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs` renders this row through the shared `judgePrompt` renderer, FORMAT.md verbatim above the input marker, and the paragraph's own input below it; `validateExtractionUnit` reads the answer back against FORMAT and `extractionFileText` writes it as FORMAT's YAML record, `<name>.yaml` (kogaki#1413), so `tools/move_ingest.py passage --from-extraction` reads it unchanged through the same YAML module; `extractionMarkdown` renders the record for reading on the Proof Sheet. The fields the Harness can count or knows -- `unit`, `length`, `status` -- and each Segment's quoted `opening` words are written by the Harness, never asked.
extraction_unit.judgment_point: write the Extraction of ONE paragraph -- `paragraph_you_must_extract` in the input -- under passages/FORMAT.md, rendered above, as a PARAGRAPH-UNIT Extraction: "The paragraph unit"'s ten rules govern, and they override the protocol's human round -- there is no step 2, no candidate is written, and you answer Q1, Q2 and Q3 yourself, one answer each (Q4 Footing is retired, and FORMAT says why). Read `earlier_paragraphs` first (rule 2): the reader you describe has just read them. Section 2: write all five reader dimensions in FORMAT's order; where `reader_state_before` is given, every row's `before` is that state copied EXACTLY, character for character (rule 3); where it is null this is the Leg's first paragraph and `before` is the state of the reader `persona` describes. `after` is the literal `unchanged` where this paragraph does not move the row, otherwise the new state in one short clause, and `segment` names the Segment number(s) after which the new state holds (rule 6). At least one row changes. Section 3: ONE SEGMENT PER SENTENCE, in the order of `sentences` -- the Harness has cut them, and your Segment N is sentence N. Each carries `content` -- what it does, written about this paragraph's own content -- `operation` -- the step's operation in one clause, stated subject-free, naming no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of your `subject_nouns`, so that it could be performed on any subject, and never its effect on the reader -- `relation` -- in your own prose, how the Segment relates to the one before it -- and `manner`. No label set is used for any of these fields. `manner` IS THE EMPTY STRING unless the Segment's technique is one `operation` and `relation` together cannot name: a local realisation the paragraph shows at that Segment, such as a brief direct statement that takes no elaboration, a quotation, or a shift of form. Empty is the normal case. A filled `manner` is one clause naming how the step is realised, never a point, never a reason, never a restatement of the `operation`, and it names no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of your `subject_nouns`. Rule 7: a section 2 `after` state is written as `operation` is, in general terms, naming no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of `subject_nouns`, and describing nothing of a neighbouring paragraph's content, so that `before` states copied from it stay general. Segment 1's `operation` carries no reference to any earlier step or earlier paragraph. A later Segment's `operation` is the operation alone, and its `relation` carries the connection to the step before. The whole record is general: every prose field of it, `operation`, `relation`, `manner`, each entry of `breaks` and each dimension state of the reader table, names no term, place, person or claim of the original, none of `subject_nouns`, and no word in the original's language; the record's `content` clause, `opening` and `obligation_content` are the only fields bound to the source. Rule 8: `obligation` IS ABSENT unless the paragraph leaves an item unexplained -- where the last Segment names a term or raises a question and no Segment gives its meaning or answer, `obligation` is the list of those items, one line each, written general in the order the paragraph names them, and `obligation_content` is the same list in the paragraph's own words, item for item; otherwise both keys are absent. Absent is the normal case, and an item any Segment's `content` clause defines or answers is never an obligation. Rule 10: `discharges` IS ABSENT unless `open_obligation` -- the earlier paragraph's items in its own words -- is given and this paragraph gives the last of its items its meaning or answer -- then `discharges` is `true`. Where `open_obligation` is null the record never carries `discharges`. Rule 9: `operation`, `content`, `relation` and `manner` describe what the sentence does when read aloud. Anything the reader would know only from the page, such as emphasis, bullets, numbering, headings, line breaks or a quotation's marks, is layout: it is recorded in `passage` and nowhere else, never in `operation`, `content`, `relation`, `manner` or a reader-state line. "Introduces a bolded term" fails the test; "introduces a term" passes it. Segment 1 carries no `relation`: its `relation` is the empty string in every paragraph, the first or a later one (rule 5), and section 1, `what_it_does`, names how the paragraph takes up the one before it. Sections 4 to 7 as FORMAT writes them; section 6, `description`, is one or two sentences telling a person reading the Move library what the paragraph does, at most 200 characters; section 7, `name`, is a snake_case verb phrase naming the transformation, not the topic, and is none of `names_taken`. Section 8, `notes`, may be empty and never carries a `split:` line: the paragraph's boundary is the source's own. Write everything in English except where you quote the paragraph.
extraction_unit.input_shape: ONE Extraction record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT, with exactly these keys: `version` "1"; `paragraph` -- the number of the paragraph in the input; `source`, `prior_text` and `language` -- FORMAT's header lines, one line each; `subject_nouns` -- an array of strings, empty for none; `answers` -- `{ "q1": <one sentence>, "q2": <one sentence>, "q3": <one sentence> }`; `what_it_does` -- section 1, one sentence; `reader` -- section 2, exactly five entries in the order knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust, each `{ "dimension": <its name>, "before": <state>, "after": "unchanged" | <new state>, "segment": <"" where after is unchanged, otherwise Segment number(s) such as "2" or "2, 3"> }`; `segments` -- section 3, one entry per sentence in order, each `{ "content": <one clause>, "operation": <one clause>, "relation": <one clause, or "" on Segment 1>, "manner": <"" unless the technique is one operation and relation cannot name, otherwise one clause> }`; `why_this_order` -- section 3's closing sentence; `presupposes` -- section 4, two or three lines as one string; `breaks` -- section 5, an array of prose tests, one or more, each one line: a specific change a careful writer might make, a dash, what the reader loses, each naming a change no other names`; `description` -- section 6, one or two sentences, at most 200 characters; `name` -- section 7; `notes` -- section 8, a string, empty for nothing. One key more, and only where rule 8 calls for it: `obligation` -- an array of one or more one-line items, each a term or a question, in the order the paragraph names them, naming no item twice, and beside it `obligation_content` -- an array of the same length, each entry that item in the paragraph's own words, one line; otherwise the record carries neither key at all. One key more, and only where rule 10 calls for it: `discharges` -- `true`, where `open_obligation` names items and this paragraph gives the last of them its meaning or answer; otherwise the record carries no `discharges` key at all. Every string is one line: no line breaks and no `|`.
extraction_unit.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; `version` not "1"; `paragraph` naming another paragraph; an empty answer or section; `reader` not the five dimensions in FORMAT's order; a `before` that differs from `reader_state_before` where one was given; a changed row naming no Segment, or a Segment number the paragraph does not have; no row changed; `segments` not one entry per sentence; a Segment missing its `content` or its `operation` clause; a Segment after the first with an empty `relation`; Segment 1 carrying a `relation`; a `manner` that restates the `operation`, adding no word of its own; a clause carrying `— operation:`, `— relation:` or `— manner:`; `breaks` not a non-empty array of one-line tests; a `subject_nouns` entry, or a word outside the Latin script, appearing in an `operation`, `relation` or `manner` clause, a `breaks` test or a reader state; a `description` over 200 characters; a `name` not in the library's id form (lower-case letters, digits and underscores) or already in `names_taken`; a `split:` line in `notes`; an `obligation` that is a map (`kind` is retired), or is not a list of one or more one-line items, or names an item twice, or names an item a Segment's `content` clause defines or answers; `obligation` or `obligation_content` without the other, or the two lists of different lengths; a `discharges` that is not `true`, or a `discharges` where `open_obligation` is null; a line break or a `|` in any string. Each refusal names the field, and is put back into your next attempt verbatim.

leg_path_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `purpose`; `rationale`; `reader_state_after` (`dimension: value` lines joined by line breaks); `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <one sentence> }` per paragraph, in order; `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>", ...] }` per paragraph, in order; and, optionally, `introduces`. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. The Harness writes `materials` (every `L<N>`) and `depends_on` (none), and no `move`, `no_move_fits`, `opens_section`, `reaches_target`, `journeys` or `reader_state_before` is composed. `leg_ids_already_carried` lists the ids earlier Legs of this Brief carry; this Leg's `leg_id` is none of them.
leg_path_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; not exactly one Leg; a Claim count, or a Leg Waypoint count, other than the paragraph count; Claim N not naming `L<N>`, or Leg Waypoint N not serving it; and the production validators over the Leg, imported: `validateLegs` (its Leg shape, the Reader start shape and its `introduces` rule, one Claim per Strand, the `reader_state_after` shape, and `waypointsRefusal` over the Leg Waypoints) -- each refused naming the Leg and, where one is at fault, the waypoint. The Section grouping and Reader target rules are whole-path rules about where a Leg sits among others and do not bind a one-Leg Brief (kogaki#1385); and the recoverability criterion (production `recoverabilityOf`, with an empty renderings record): a word of a Claim's `proposition` or a Leg Waypoint's `point` that is in no Segment `content` of the paragraph it serves, in no `introduces` entry and is not a function word, refused naming the word and the Segments (kogaki#1495). Each refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim.
